stories.title: Why BITS Pilani rebuilt its undergraduate curriculum
stories.summary: AI, shifting industry needs and student wellbeing pushed BITS Pilani to rethink its undergraduate courses, with more hands-on learning, design and problem-solving and changes to academic workload. It is also spending INR 50 crore on lab upgrades across Pilani, Goa and Hyderabad.

stories.title: Jharkhand schools team up to make vocational courses a first choice
stories.summary: The Jharkhand Education Project Council has signed an MoU with IPE Global to strengthen vocational training for Classes 9 to 12 in government schools, with a focus on girls. The plan covers career awareness, on-the-job training and core employability skills.

stories.title: HITSEEE 2027 registration opens on 4 November
stories.summary: Hindustan Institute of Technology and Science will take applications for its BTech, BArch and BDes entrance exam from 4 November until 21 April 2027, with the exam from 28 April. Candidates must be at least 16 years and six months old under the stated rule.

stories.title: An Ohio district trains teens for careers fighting hackers
stories.summary: In Ohio's Lakota district, students can take cybersecurity classes from sophomore year, learning how websites get hacked and how to stop it. Many network with industry professionals and earn certifications before turning 18, and some treat it as the start of a career.

stories.title: Grade 9 students like science more when it feels useful
stories.summary: A study of 382 Grade 9 students in UAE public schools, plus focus groups, looked at how everyday relevance and career awareness link to interest in school science and STEM ambitions. Knowing where science leads seems to keep teenagers interested in it.

stories.title: From a Year 10 science camp to a neuroscience PhD
stories.summary: Sarah Domoney attended the John Innes Centre's Year 10 Science Camp in 2015 and is now working towards a PhD at UCL's Queen Square Institute of Neurology. She says the lab tutorials, learning to use pipettes with real scientists, were the highlight.

stories.title: Vietnam's top IT graduate had a job lined up six months early
stories.summary: Nguyen Dang Minh, 23, graduated top of his class at the Posts and Telecommunications Institute of Technology with a 3.85 GPA, after securing a job at a major US tech company. He credits university research labs and projects for the hands-on experience.

stories.title: A Nebraska deal guarantees community college students a university place
stories.summary: Southeast Community College students who earn an associate degree with at least a 2.0 GPA are guaranteed admission to the University of Nebraska-Lincoln. The On Course partnership maps more than 50 transfer pathways so students know how credits will count.

stories.title: Arunachal Class 9 student wins a prize at the National Science Seminar
stories.summary: Rubu Daniel of Vivekananda Kendra Vidyalaya, Oyan, placed among the top nine runners-up at the National Science Seminar 2026 in New Delhi, competing against students from 34 states and union territories. He received a special prize and a one-year scholarship of Rs 24,000.

stories.title: A Delhi teen built a robot after spotting litter beside bins
stories.summary: On a 2023 school trip to Sundar Nursery, Mahi Malhani, now 17, noticed rubbish lying a few steps from dustbins. Instead of blaming behaviour, she asked how technology could help and went on to develop TRASHbot, an AI robot that detects, collects and sorts waste.

stories.title: Indore teens built a fridge that runs on salt and water
stories.summary: Dhruv Chaudhary, Mithran Ladhania and Mridul Jain designed Thermavault, which uses the cooling effect of dissolving salts to keep vaccines cold without electricity. It won the Earth Prize for Asia and $12,500, which they plan to use to make 200 units for 120 hospitals.

stories.title: Turkish students turned tarantula venom into a wound gel
stories.summary: Inspired by a grandmother's bedsores, İrfan Sefiloğlu and İrem Alparslan of Erzurum BİLSEM developed a hydrogel from Cuban tarantula venom that showed positive results in cell tests. It placed second at the TÜBİTAK final, and they head to Regeneron ISEF in 2027.

stories.title: A New Zealand teen built a tool to help his uncle join conversations
stories.summary: Jack Harker, a Year 11 student at ACG Parnell College in Auckland, developed Parley to help people who struggle to speak take part in real-time conversations. His uncle has cerebral palsy. The project won its category at Samsung Solve for Tomorrow New Zealand.

stories.title: A Hanoi student wins a global robotics badge
stories.summary: Tran Phuong Thao of Hanoi-Amsterdam High School was the only Vietnamese student to receive the You Inspire Me badge at the FIRST Tech Challenge, where her team was division runner-up. She has now received Hanoi's Living Beautifully Youth award.

stories.title: A 15-year-old in Benin wins a global letter-writing prize
stories.summary: Marie-Ange Chekpo won fourth prize worldwide and the national first prize at the 55th Universal Postal Union letter-writing competition, which asked young people to reflect on relationships in the digital age. The contest drew 1.48 million entrants from 65 countries.

stories.title: Spring Grove's rocketry team is heading to NASA Student Launch
stories.summary: The Pennsylvania high school team is one of 17 picked nationwide for NASA's Student Launch after a 47-page proposal. Students will spend months designing, building and testing a rocket of about ten feet before the finals in Alabama in April.

stories.title: Two French teens turned a class project into an award-winning revision app
stories.summary: Lucas Gerhardt and Clément Bellet-Odent, both 18, built LUCID at Henri Matisse High School in Vence to help students revise at their own pace with flashcards, quizzes and an AI tutor. It has won recognition in France and Europe.

stories.title: Two Kealakehe High graduates named US Presidential Scholars
stories.summary: Daniel Chen and Zachariah Smith are the first pair from the same Hawaii public school to win the honour in one year. They were among 161 high school seniors nationwide recognised for academics, the arts and career and technical education.

stories.title: Two Lemont students score a perfect 36 on the ACT
stories.summary: Matthew Butler and Ishan Samani of Lemont High School in Illinois each scored 36 in April, joining just 11 students in the school's history to do so. Fewer than two-tenths of one percent of ACT takers reach the top score.

stories.title: Glossopdale sixth formers complete their Gold DofE expedition
stories.summary: Five students became the first sixth-form team at the school to take on the Gold Duke of Edinburgh's Award in more than 20 years. They practised in the Peak District in July heat and finished their qualifying expedition in the Lake District.

stories.title: Wirral pupils win a national award for social action
stories.summary: Students at St John Plessington Catholic College in Bebington received CAFOD's LiveSimply Award for two years of projects caring for people and the planet. Head of religious education Carmel Harvey called it a testament to the whole school community.

stories.title: Pune scientists find a galaxy whose black hole woke up four times
stories.summary: Researchers from IISER Pune and NCRA-TIFR found an S-shaped radio galaxy about 4.2 million light-years across showing four separate episodes of activity from its central black hole. It is the first known galaxy with evidence of four such cycles.

stories.title: Indian scientists name a new electric ray from the Arabian Sea
stories.summary: The Zoological Survey of India described Tetronarce ramanamurthyi, the Arabian Black Electric Ray, from nine specimens collected in deep waters off India's southwestern coast. It adds to what we know about life in the northern Indian Ocean.

stories.title: Mizoram University researchers find a new gecko in Assam
stories.summary: The new species was found in the rocky habitats of Umrangso in Assam's Dima Hasao district, state Forest Minister Jayanta Malla Baruah said. It is a reminder that plenty of wildlife is still waiting to be noticed.

stories.title: A giant new dwarf planet candidate may lurk beyond Pluto
stories.summary: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory has found its first candidate dwarf planet in the dark, cold region beyond Pluto, ScienceAlert reports. Scientists have long pieced this zone together from scattered clues, and Rubin is expected to reveal far more of it.

stories.title: Hubble and Webb team up to find 27 tiny worlds beyond Neptune
stories.summary: Using both telescopes together for the first time on trans-Neptunian objects, astronomers found 27 new icy bodies. The smallest is about 5 kilometres across, roughly five times smaller than the faintest object the best telescope on Earth can detect.

stories.title: Astronauts complete the 100th US spacewalk from the ISS
stories.summary: NASA's Anil Menon and Canada's Joshua Kutryk spent 7 hours and 11 minutes outside the space station on 29 October, installing and deploying the second-to-last upgraded solar array. The station now has more power.

stories.title: NASA's year-long mock Mars mission comes to an end
stories.summary: Four volunteers of the CHAPEA mission 2 crew left NASA's 3D-printed Mars habitat in Houston after 378 days. Ross Elder, Matthew Montgomery, Ellen Ellis and James Spicer ran simulated Mars operations from a 1,700 sq ft home on Earth.

stories.title: NASA's Lucy reaches Jupiter's asteroid swarms
stories.summary: Five years and more than 2.2 billion miles after launch, Lucy has become the first spacecraft to reach the groups of asteroids that share Jupiter's orbit, one swarm ahead of the planet and one behind it.

stories.title: Jumping spiders may dream
stories.summary: University of Bonn researchers found Australian jumping spiders have two stages of sleep, including one much like human REM sleep with twitching muscles and moving eyes. It raises the question of whether spiders experience something like dreams.

stories.title: Betelgeuse's companion star leaves a wake through its atmosphere
stories.summary: Radio observations show Siwarha, the smaller companion of the red supergiant Betelgeuse about 650 light-years away, cutting through the big star's extended atmosphere and leaving a trail like a boat on a lake.

stories.title: Scientists identify Yak X, a lost Ice Age relative of yaks
stories.summary: Researchers studying 20 small bone fragments from Denisova Cave in Siberia's Altai Mountains identified an extinct animal closely related to today's yaks. It lived alongside woolly mammoths and woolly rhinos and went unnoticed until now.

stories.title: Fossils reveal an amphibian that lived in the sea
stories.summary: Two skeletons from China show Gerrothorax maritimus, an armoured amphibian nearly three feet long that lived on the seafloor about 237 million years ago. No amphibian alive today can live entirely in salt water.

stories.title: Some dying stars glow pink and green
stories.summary: Astronomers have found white dwarfs, the dense leftovers of sun-like stars, that do not look white at all. Most star colours come from temperature, so these pink and green ones are an exception scientists are now studying.

stories.title: Healthy corals may help bleached ones recover
stories.summary: In a study in Science Advances, scientists placed a healthy coral next to an identical bleached one. After a couple of weeks the bleached coral had almost fully recovered, which could help reefs threatened by rising sea temperatures.

stories.title: How to practise for RMO problems that go beyond the textbook
stories.summary: Regional Mathematical Olympiad questions often need several ideas joined together, and no formula fits directly. The advice is to practise non-routine problems often, break hard questions into smaller steps, compare different solution methods and review mistakes.

stories.title: How the CBSE Class 12 chemistry paper is laid out
stories.summary: The 2027 theory paper carries 70 marks over three hours, with 30 more for practical and project assessment. It has multiple choice and assertion-reasoning questions, very short and short answers, case-based questions and long answers, and daily sample papers are suggested.

stories.title: Learning to persuade without selling out
stories.summary: Students pitch projects, interview for scholarships, present research and defend proposals every semester, so persuasion matters, The Hindu argues. Success depends on presenting an idea with credibility and purpose, not only on how good the idea is.

stories.title: A Class 9 student asks how to combine psychology, crime and writing
stories.summary: Samreen loves psychology, criminology, toxicology and storytelling but is told to pick a secure career. The Hindu's counsellor says she has time, and points to interdisciplinary fields such as forensic psychology and criminal profiling.

stories.title: Over 800 players sign up for the Maharashtra schools chess championship
stories.summary: The SBI Life Maharashtra State Schools Chess Championship has a record 800 plus players from over 500 schools, including more than 400 FIDE-rated. It runs at Rustomjee Cambridge International School, Dahisar, from 4 to 6 and 13 to 15 November.

stories.title: GD Goenka Srinagar wraps up its model UN
stories.summary: The two-day GDGS MUN 2026 at GD Goenka Public School, Srinagar, ended on 30 October with delegates from several schools debating pressing global issues over two days and practising diplomacy, dialogue, negotiation and consensus-building. It closed with a felicitation ceremony for the young delegates.

stories.title: Samsung Solve for Tomorrow Vietnam names its winners
stories.summary: The top 17 teams presented STEM solutions to community problems at the final in Vietnam on 31 October, held with the National Innovation Center. Projects covered the environment, sport and technology, and education.

stories.title: A Ghana technical school wins a renewable energy challenge by one point
stories.summary: Dabokpa Technical Institute scored 83 to win the Northern Zone of the Energy Commission's challenge for senior high schools. Yaa Asantewaa Girls SHS took second with 82 for a solar-powered vaccine cooler.

stories.title: A Lagos school team wins Zecathon and ₦5 million
stories.summary: Four students from Caleb British International School, Abijo, won the Zenith Bank Future Innovators Challenge, Zecathon 6.0, with a project called ReLearn. The school took the ₦5 million grand prize against finalists from across Nigeria.

stories.title: Six Lagos students win prizes in a green essay contest
stories.summary: The Society for Environmental Toxicology and Pollution Mitigation awarded cash prizes in junior and senior categories. Oyenike Adeyemi of Methodist Girls' High School won the junior section and N100,000, with Faridah Moshood of Daltha Heights School second on N70,000.

stories.title: Slovakia's young science winners are off to Kazakhstan
stories.summary: The BARS5 science competition final drew teams from 228 secondary school students. A Bratislava team won the main prize, a month-long research expedition to Kazakhstan with field work in nature reserves alongside scientists.

stories.title: Marshall University opens registration for its High School Science Day
stories.summary: The 2027 event on 12 April at the Huntington campus in West Virginia brings STEM students together to connect classroom ideas to everyday life. Organiser Sean McBride calls it a fun way for students to explore science.

stories.title: NMMSS applications are open until 15 November
stories.summary: The Education Ministry has extended the National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship deadline for 2026-27 on the National Scholarship Portal. By 30 October, 90,483 fresh and 1,99,531 renewal applications had come in. The scheme offers one lakh fresh scholarships.

stories.title: Tata Capital Pankh scholarship offers up to ₹18,000
stories.summary: Students from economically weaker sections in Class 11 and 12, undergraduate, diploma and ITI courses can apply for support covering 80% to 100% of tuition fees up to the cap. The last date to apply online is 15 November.

stories.title: Rajasthan extends its scholarship deadline to 31 December
stories.summary: The Social Justice and Empowerment Department moved the 2026-27 registration and application deadline from 31 October to 31 December. Institutions can complete registration, renewals, course mapping and fee details on the portal in the meantime.

stories.title: Scholarships for Indian students cover tuition and coaching in 2026-27
stories.summary: A roundup lists programmes from foundations, companies and charities for students from poorer families, girls in higher education, medical aspirants and students with disabilities. Benefits range from full tuition support to free competitive exam coaching.

stories.title: Taco Bell's Live Más Scholarship opens with $13 million
stories.summary: The Taco Bell Foundation's 12th round awards $5,000, $10,000 and $25,000 to US students aged 16 to 25. Applicants need no grades, test scores or resumes, only a two-minute video or a short essay about their passion.

stories.title: Dalhousie welcomes two new Schulich Leaders
stories.summary: Chinazam Igwe and Joseph Fay, first-year computer science and engineering students, are the university's 49th and 50th Schulich Leader Scholars. They were among 100 picked from 350,000 graduating high school students and 1,300 nominations.

stories.title: Two Cambodian students win ASEAN Scholarships to Singapore
stories.summary: Sa Sokritthi and Sok Moniketsya passed several rounds of assessment to win the four-year scholarship, which covers secondary and pre-university study in Singapore leading to the Singapore-Cambridge GCE A-Level certificate. It is open to students from ASEAN countries.

stories.title: HKUST adds an interdisciplinary degree and bigger scholarships
stories.summary: More than 55,000 students, parents and educators attended HKUST's undergraduate information day. For 2027/28 entry the university highlighted a standalone admission route for its individualised interdisciplinary major, which lets students design their own learning path.

stories.title: JEE Main 2027 applicants can file a fresh form but must pay again
stories.summary: NTA says Session 1 candidates who made errors may submit a fresh application even if they already paid, but the earlier fee will not be refunded or adjusted. Only the last paid application will count.

stories.title: JEE aspirants petition for a third attempt at JEE Advanced
stories.summary: An online petition with 13,000 signatures argues the two-attempt limit disadvantages students in regular schooling. It also asks for two attempts spread over three consecutive years, saying the current rule hurts students trying for seats at the IITs.

stories.title: Assam lets 2026 HS pass-outs sit the 2027 exam to improve marks
stories.summary: ASSEB will allow students who passed the 2026 HS Final to take the 2027 exam for betterment, after requests from those needing higher marks for NEET-UG and engineering entrance exams. They can retake all subjects or a few.

stories.title: Telangana may bring Inter exams forward to 24 February
stories.summary: Theory papers for the 2027 Intermediate exams may begin on 24 February, with practicals from 1 February, including for first-year MPC and BiPC students. The board has not yet released the official timetable, so dates could change.

stories.title: Juneau PSAT maths scores drop as more students take AP exams
stories.summary: Only 26% of 10th graders met the PSAT maths benchmark in Juneau, Alaska, and the district average has fallen 41 points since 2023. Students taking AP exams earned qualifying scores on nearly three quarters of their tests.

stories.title: NMC gives two different answers on Georgia MBBS degrees
stories.summary: Two aspiring doctors asked the National Medical Commission whether a six-year MBBS from Georgia qualifies for the Foreign Medical Graduate Examination and got conflicting replies. The mix-up has raised worries about students being misled when choosing colleges abroad.

stories.title: Cambridge plans closer ties with India
stories.summary: Vice chancellor Deborah Prentice told Eastern Eye that the university wants to strengthen its long relationship with India. One plan has Cambridge Judge Business School offering certificates to students in India, with two weeks of teaching in India by its academics.

stories.title: Applications open for a week at CERN for high school students
stories.summary: The A&A Excursion to CERN 2027, from 13 to 19 June, takes 15 high school and undergraduate students interested in physics and astronomy to Geneva for lectures, lab visits, workshops and a group project. Applications close on 27 December.

stories.title: The UK's £925 student levy starts in August 2028
stories.summary: The UK plans an annual levy of £925 per eligible international student. Nigeria's Petroleum Technology Development Fund, which has sponsored nearly 15,000 students, has pointed to Germany and France as alternatives as costs and visa delays rise.

stories.title: Australia plans to rethink student visa rules
stories.summary: The government wants to balance strict eligibility with attracting good applicants after high refusal rates for students from South Asia. The rejections trace back to a ministerial direction two years ago checking that study is the real motive.

stories.title: Australia's student visa review could change access for African applicants
stories.summary: Public universities could lose A$2 billion over three years after a fall in enrolments, and more than 52% of offshore Kenyan applications were rejected in 2025/26. Officials warn clearer rules may still mean higher financial thresholds.

stories.title: Canada's Express Entry changes from 3 November
stories.summary: New rules favour skilled Indian professionals with Canadian work experience or high-wage job offers, while applicants moving straight from India may find it harder to compete for permanent residency. Students planning to stay on after study may want to note it.

stories.title: Nepal's medical colleges struggle to attract foreign students
stories.summary: Nepal reserves a third of its medical seats for foreign students, but only 746 enrolled last year. This year 176 foreign candidates, including from India, Bangladesh and the Maldives, will sit the entrance exam.

stories.title: Jashpur brings AI, coding and robotics to government school students
stories.summary: Chhattisgarh's Jashpur district has signed an MoU with Edu Roboverse for a year-long programme in AI, coding, robotics and machine learning for Classes 9 to 12 in three government schools. Students will build sensor-driven smart systems.

stories.title: Google adds free textbooks to Gemini Notebook
stories.summary: Students in India and the US can now open hundreds of free textbooks inside Gemini Notebook, ask questions about them and make study guides, practice quizzes and flashcards. Google announced the feature on 29 October at no extra cost.

stories.title: Vietnam launches a free AI test for every high school student
stories.summary: Viettel and IIG Vietnam launched the AI or Behind competition on 31 October, the first in the country to use an internationally standardised AI test, provided by Pearson-Certiport. It is free for high school students nationwide.

stories.title: Hong Kong primary pupils will study AI in a new subject
stories.summary: A new information and innovation technology subject will roll out in Hong Kong primary schools from September 2028. Children as young as seven will hold simple conversations with an AI system using prompts and commands.

stories.title: Hong Kong pupils learn budgeting with an AI digital pet
stories.summary: At SKH Kei Oi Primary School, a teacher built a virtual pet with AI and web tools for a lesson on saving, and Primary Two pupils debated whether it needed meal vouchers or game cards. Teachers say assessing work has become harder.

stories.title: A Guelph school board invites students to join its FIRST Robotics Team
stories.summary: Upper Grand students in Grades 9 to 12 can design and program robots with industry mentors, or take on media and marketing roles. A parent and student open house is on 4 November at College Heights SS.

stories.title: Nucor backs youth robotics in Nebraska
stories.summary: The steelmaker has invested $250,000 in the Northeast iHub and sponsored its first robotics team four years ago, giving young people hands-on time with robots and technology that could lead to careers in manufacturing and engineering.

stories.title: Vietnamese parents worry about children leaning on AI
stories.summary: PISA results released in September show up to 94% of Vietnamese students use AI chatbots for learning. A Hanoi parent says her children are glued to devices during homework and she cannot tell if AI is doing the work.

stories.title: A school's AI image of a six-year-old's future self worries her mother
stories.summary: Nikki Anderson's daughter came home with an AI picture of herself at 25 as a nurse. The Charleston mother asked about consent, the tool used and the uploaded data, and an expert says AI is already in everyday learning tools.

stories.title: Dutch MPs call for a ban on generative AI in primary schools
stories.summary: A motion backed by parties with 88 of 150 seats asks the cabinet to bar tools like ChatGPT for primary pupils, saying they threaten basic reading, writing and critical thinking skills.

stories.title: J&K teachers say Holistic Progress Cards lack training and support
stories.summary: Government school teachers in Jammu and Kashmir say the NEP 2020 progress cards, meant to assess children beyond marks, have become form filling. They cite poor training, gaps in digital infrastructure and pressure to complete online entries alone.

stories.title: A learning software veteran on making sure every child learns
stories.summary: Writing in The 74, a developer who has built learning software for 25 years, starting with a CD-ROM in a McGraw-Hill textbook, says tools have changed from discs to AI while the way people learn has not.

stories.title: Massachusetts names a dual-language kindergarten teacher Teacher of the Year
stories.summary: Desirée Garcia of German Gerena Community School in Springfield teaches young children in Spanish and English while encouraging pride in their cultures. She is the 2027 Massachusetts Teacher of the Year.

stories.title: A Mahopac German teacher wins a national award
stories.summary: The American Association of Teachers of German named Katrina Bauerlein its 2026 Outstanding German Educator for high schools, its highest honour. She has taught at Mahopac since 2001 after a Fulbright year in Germany.

stories.title: In the age of AI, learning still needs friction
stories.summary: Grainger Engineering at Illinois says AI may change how engineers work but cannot replace what they know, understand or answer for. Its faculty are building AI fluency into courses without lowering rigour.

stories.title: Canterbury College teachers build AI skills together
stories.summary: At Canterbury College in Queensland, Microsoft's Elevate for Educators programme helps teachers move from trying AI to leading with it through professional learning, collaboration and sharing what works. The idea is that AI's real potential in classrooms starts with teachers who feel confident using it.

stories.title: New Zealand teachers will decide how to fit farming into Year 11 science
stories.summary: With Year 11 agricultural and horticultural science dropped as a standalone subject and science made compulsory, schools must include agriculture on their own initiative. A Food and Fibre Systems subject for Years 12 and 13 is planned from 2029.

stories.title: Shalee Hodgson wins a national award for evaluating technical education
stories.summary: EvaluATE, the hub for the National Science Foundation's Advanced Technological Education programme, gave the Fosston High School graduate its Outstanding ATE Evaluation Award for rigorous, clear assessment of technical education and workforce training programmes.

stories.title: Singapore principals say look beyond PSLE cut-off points
stories.summary: At a Straits Times forum, five principals urged parents not to choose secondary schools by PSLE scores alone, since results may not show true ability. They suggested using all six choices well, attending open houses and talking to students.

stories.title: GEMS Education redesigns the school day for the AI era
stories.summary: Dubai-based GEMS has unveiled GR8 School, a model combining AI-powered personalised learning with teacher support, industry expertise and hands-on experiences. It aims to rethink what children learn for, as well as how.

stories.title: Nearly a third of school leaders skip AI for operations
stories.summary: An EdWeek survey looks at whether districts use generative AI beyond teaching, for jobs like budgets and administration. Nearly one in three district and school leaders say they do not use it for operations at all.

stories.title: Big US districts tell the FCC not to use E-rate to police screen time
stories.summary: Districts from New York City to Dallas filed comments in the FCC's review of the roughly $3 billion a year E-rate programme, which helps schools pay for internet. Most support the programme but oppose using it to regulate classroom screen time.

stories.title: UNT launches a network to tackle a dual credit teacher shortage
stories.summary: Texas faces an estimated 15% gap between student demand for dual credit courses and qualified instructors, says Rudi Thompson of the University of North Texas. UNT's new statewide Dual Credit Network aims to close it.

stories.title: Unqualified teachers in Nunavut nearly doubled in five years
stories.summary: Ninety-three of more than 800 teachers now work under one-year letters of authority. Education Minister David Akeeagok says he is not concerned, calling it a small share that reflects the need to keep schools running.

stories.title: Maldives plans clear rules for home-schooling
stories.summary: Education Minister Ismail Shafeeu says an amendment to the Education Act will set legal rules for home-schooling so no student is excluded from learning. Home-based learning will follow an assessment of each applicant's needs.

stories.title: Everett schools plan an IB diploma programme for 2027
stories.summary: Everett Public Schools in Washington is moving ahead with plans for an International Baccalaureate diploma programme at Cascade High School, open to students across the district, pending final approval. The courses would let high schoolers earn college credit at the same time.

stories.title: Regenesys Online School prepares to open in Johannesburg
stories.summary: The Sandton-based school will welcome its first learners in January 2027 and has registered more than 100 already. It will offer Cambridge International and South Africa's CAPS pathways as another option for secondary education.

stories.title: King's College Wimbledon's Ho Chi Minh City campus tops out
stories.summary: The campus finished its main structure on 25 October and plans to open in August 2027 for about 1,500 students on 1.8 hectares. It is being developed with King's College School, Wimbledon.

stories.title: Karnataka drafts rules to limit coaching centres
stories.summary: Proposed rules would bar coaching institutes from admitting children under 15, cap daily coaching at five hours and require fee refunds for students who leave midway. The state wants to ease academic pressure and curb misleading advertising.

stories.title: KVS will launch a Samvaad app for parents
stories.summary: Parents of students at more than 1,200 Kendriya Vidyalayas will soon see attendance, academic performance and school announcements on their phones through the KVS Samvaad-Parent Connect App, without waiting for parent-teacher meetings.

stories.title: A film on Bihar's girls' education movement wins a UN award
stories.summary: Mothers of Courage, about a women-led grassroots push for girls' education in Bihar, won the 2026 UN SDG Action Award for Creativity in Rome on 29 October. It was chosen from over 7,000 entries from 190 countries.

stories.title: BASF Kids' Lab brings chemistry to 1,150 Hyderabad children
stories.summary: BASF and CSIR-IICT ran hands-on chemistry experiments and climate awareness sessions for municipal school children aged eight to 12 from 26 to 31 October. Small lab coats, presumably, were involved.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu's government ITIs get advanced skill centres
stories.summary: Schneider Electric India Foundation will set up 70 advanced training centres in Tamil Nadu's government ITIs to train about 25,000 young people. Thirty centres are already open and 40 more are proposed.

stories.title: Thrissur students return from a NASA study tour
stories.summary: Eighteen students from Classes 10 to 12 at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan schools in Thrissur, with a teacher, completed a 10-day tour of the US that included a visit to NASA's Kennedy Space Center and a meeting with a veteran astronaut.

stories.title: November brings a run of school holidays
stories.summary: Diwali, Govardhan Puja, Bhai Dooj, Chhath Puja and Guru Nanak Jayanti all fall in November 2026. Several land on weekdays, giving students in some states extra breaks from regular classes.

events.line: School leaders on international curricula and study abroad.

events.line: Free Cambridge English teacher webinar on why assessment matters for opportunity and lifelong learning. Second sitting 5 Nov at 9:30 PM IST.

events.time: 2:30 AM IST next day (4:00 to 6:00 PM ET)
events.line: A Zoom workshop for grades 3 to 12 teachers on turning texts into audio, video and mind maps. Hosted by Nextech.

events.time: 4:00 AM IST next day (4:00 PM ET)
events.line: Free UMaine Extension Zoom series for ages 9 to 12 on how models make predictions.

events.line: Free Zoom PD from Chatteris and Nord Anglia on Thrive Approach strategies for emotional regulation in primary classrooms.

events.line: ACAMH clinical webinar on adolescent sleep problems for mental health professionals.
